2.1 Instalando quarto, python, julia
Puedes usar Quarto en GitHub Codespaces de manera excelente, ya que ofrece un entorno preconfigurado basado en VS Code que elimina la instalación local.
En la raíz de tu repositorio crea la carpeta:
devcontainer.json
Dockerfile
No instalamos Quarto ni Julia aquí porque es mucho más sencillo mantenerlos actualizados desde el script.
postCreate.sh

title: 2  Chapter: Basic Tools
text:
Crear un nuevo repo en GitHub
Abre codespace en el main
Lo primero es tener instalada la extensión “Quarto” de quarto-dev en tu VS Code o codespaces (el ícono de cuadrícula en la barra lateral izquierda o Ctrl+Shift+X). Esta extensión es la que provee el soporte de lenguaje, incluyendo el resaltado de sintaxis para los bloques de código de Python, R, Julia y otros
Para que el resaltado y la inteligencia de código funcionen perfectamente para Python y Julia, necesitas tener instaladas las extensiones de esos lenguajes

Para Python: La extensión oficial de Python de Microsoft (ms-python.python).
Para Julia: La extensión oficial de Julia de julialang (julialang.language-julia).

Ahora es importante instalar quarto (prueba hasta quarto check). Usa chatgpt para buscar la versión actualizada y como instalar

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ wget https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.10.15/quarto-1.10.15-linux-amd64.deb
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ sudo dpkg -i quarto-1.10.15-linux-amd64.deb
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ quarto --version
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ quarto check

Usualmente python ya viene instalado, si quieres instalar una versión más actualizada vete a tomar por culo y busca la versión que quieres en chatgpt jaja. Instalamos jupyter luego.

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ pip install jupyter

Instalaremos la versión más estable de Julia

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ source ~/.bashrc
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ julia --version
julia version 1.12.6
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add("IJulia")

Si eres un pesaooo y quieres la última versión de la web estable de Julia, aqui tienes los comandos gilipollas jaja.

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ wget https://julialang-s3.julialang.org/bin/linux/x64/1.12/julia-1.12.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ tar -xzf julia-1.12.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ sudo mv julia-1.12.1 /opt/julia
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ echo 'export PATH="/opt/julia/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ source ~/.bashrc
@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ julia --version

Como vas a desarrollar un libro técnico de Data Science, Python, Julia, SQL, Power BI y mercados eléctricos durante bastante tiempo, conviene que no instales Quarto y Julia manualmente cada vez que crees un Codespace. Lo más práctico es crear un .devcontainer que instale automáticamente. De esa forma, tendrás un entorno completamente reproducible: cualquier Codespace que abras tendrá automáticamente Quarto, Julia, Python, Jupyter y las extensiones de VS Code sin ejecutar ningún comando manual.


.devcontainer/
├── devcontainer.json
├── Dockerfile
└── postCreate.sh

{
    "name": "Quarto Data Science Book",

    "build": {
        "dockerfile": "Dockerfile"
    },

    "customizations": {
        "vscode": {
            "settings": {
                "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "/usr/local/bin/python3",
                "jupyter.askForKernelRestart": false,
                "editor.wordWrap": "on"
            },

            "extensions": [
                "quarto.quarto",
                "ms-python.python",
                "ms-toolsai.jupyter",
                "julialang.language-julia",
                "yzhang.markdown-all-in-one",
                "DavidAnson.vscode-markdownlint",
                "GitHub.copilot",
                "GitHub.copilot-chat",
                "eamodio.gitlens"
            ]
        }
    },

    "postCreateCommand": "bash .devcontainer/postCreate.sh",

    "remoteUser": "vscode"
}

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
        wget \
        curl \
        git \
        unzip \
        build-essential \
        pandoc \
        texlive-latex-base \
        texlive-fonts-recommended \
        texlive-latex-extra \
        texlive-xetex \
        fonts-dejavu && \
    apt-get clean


#!/bin/bash

set -e

echo "====================================="
echo "Installing Quarto"
echo "====================================="

QUARTO_VERSION="1.10.15"

wget https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v${QUARTO_VERSION}/quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}-linux-amd64.deb

sudo dpkg -i quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}-linux-amd64.deb

rm quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}-linux-amd64.deb

echo "====================================="
echo "Installing Julia"
echo "====================================="

curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh -s -- --yes

export PATH="$HOME/.juliaup/bin:$PATH"

echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.juliaup/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc

source ~/.bashrc

echo "====================================="
echo "Installing Python packages"
echo "====================================="

pip install --upgrade pip

pip install \
    jupyter \
    jupyterlab \
    notebook \
    numpy \
    scipy \
    pandas \
    matplotlib \
    seaborn \
    scikit-learn \
    plotly \
    polars \
    pyarrow \
    duckdb

echo "====================================="
echo "Installing Julia packages"
echo "====================================="

~/.juliaup/bin/julia <<EOF
using Pkg

Pkg.add([
    "IJulia",
    "DataFrames",
    "CSV",
    "Plots",
    "Statistics",
    "Distributions",
    "GLM",
    "DataFramesMeta",
    "DuckDB"
])

EOF

echo "====================================="
echo "Checking installations"
echo "====================================="

quarto --version

python --version

~/.juliaup/bin/julia --version

quarto check

echo "Environment ready!"

Dar permisos al script, solo la primera vez.

@yachasun40 ➜ /workspaces/power_systems_analysis (main) $ chmod +x .devcontainer/postCreate.sh

Cuando GitHub detecte la carpeta .devcontainer, al crear un nuevo Codespace:

Construirá el contenedor.
Ejecutará postCreate.sh.
Instalará automáticamente:

Ahora sí mamón, esto es super importante para que guardes en GitHub todos los cambios que hiciste en tus ficheros y en tu repo, no lo olvides. Elimina primero los instaladores .deb que descargaste en codespaces, ya que GitHub no permite archivos mayores de 100 MB.

git add .
git commit -m "Add devcontainer"
git push

3.1.1 Reading and Writing Files with Open
File handling is an essential aspect of programming, and Python provides built-in functions to interact with files. This guide will explore how to use Python’s open function to read the text files (‘.txt’ files).
There are two methods for opening the file using the file handling concept.

Using the open() function without a context manager.

File path: The file path parameter consists of the filename and directory where the file is located.
Mode: The mode parameter specifies the purpose of opening the file, such as ‘r’ for reading, ‘w’ for writing, or ‘a’ for appending.
# Open the file in read ('r') mode
file = open('file.txt', 'r')

4.1 Introduction to Databases and SQL
Welcome to the “SQL Fundamentals” course! In today’s world, data is a critical business asset. But, if we can’t tap into that data, if we can’t access and manipulate it, it’s wasted. SQL solves that problem. It’s a language of databases. It allows you to communicate with a database and get what you need. It’s a critical skill in every analyst or data scientist’s toolbox, and it appears on most job postings for those positions. You’re going to develop that skill within this course. By the end, you will learn to construct a wide variety of SQL statements. By the end, you will learn to construct a wide variety of SQL statements. We start with the basics, and then move to more advanced concepts – like joins, subqueries, common table expressions, and window functions. Finally, you’ll also learn how to optimize your SQL statements so they’re efficient even on extremely large data sets.

The idea of supply chains is managing flows. And flows of what? Flows of product or material, flows of information, and flows of money.
Course Overview and Basic Tools
starts by providing a fundamental grounding in combinatorics, and then quickly moves into the basics of probability theory. Finally, the last third of the class will focus on data analysis and machine learning as a means for seeing direct applications of probability in this exciting and quickly growing subfield of computer science.

title: 7  Data Visualization and Cloud Technologies
text:
In this course, we learn to use data visualization and cloud computing to support business analytics. In the cloud computing section, we use the cloud to build scalable data warehouses, analyze big data, and develop machine learning models. In the data visualization section, we create and share compelling visualizations that enhance decision-making.
In the first half of the course, you’ll learn how to tell compelling stories using data visualization. Then in the second half, we’ll learning about cloud computing. You’ll set up and manage a cloud data warehouse, build and deploy a machine learning model in the cloud, and analyze big data in a cloud environment. These skills will prepare you to add value to your career right away.

title: 8  Capítulo: Data Science with R
text:
8.1 Data Science
Data science is a multidisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data. It combines aspects of statistics, computer science, and domain expertise to analyze and interpret complex data sets. Data scientists use various tools and techniques to clean, process, and analyze data, often employing machine learning algorithms to make predictions or uncover patterns. The goal of data science is to turn data into actionable insights that can inform decision-making and drive business strategies. It is widely used in various industries, including finance, healthcare, marketing, and technology, to solve complex problems and improve outcomes.
